transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-09-24
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes (approx)
Recording: Yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Ethan Park (Redwood CSM); Priya Rao (NexaHead ML), Liam O'Connor (Platform), Sara Kim (Security), Jamal Ahmed (DevOps)

Summary:
Quick sync on onboarding progress, access setup, and environment readiness. SE to run benchmark with 8k context, security to review SOC2 docs, confirm VPC peering and IAM, then reconvene next week.

Topics:
- Access & infra (VPC peering, IAM, SSO)
- Benchmark plan and metrics (p90 latency, throughput, cost)
- Security/compliance (SOC2, encryption, audit logs)
- Next steps and timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: okay hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. I'll kick off, this is our weekly poc sync for Nexa, um, quick roll call?
[00:07] Priya: yep Priya here, hi.
[00:09] Liam: Liam on platform.
[00:10] Sara: Sara, security.
[00:12] Jamal: Jamal, DevOps.
[00:14] Diego: Diego, SE at Redwood.
[00:16] Maya: sweet, quick agenda, access, benchmarks, and security. Diego you wanna take benchmarks?
[00:22] Diego: yeah sure, um so recapping from last week, we got the sample prompts and some infra details, we still need the VPC peering info from Jamal, and we need to confirm the tokenization settings, oh and the KV cache preference - I think you mentioned you'd prefer persistent caching?
[00:38] Jamal: yeah we can do persistent, but need details on traffic egress, and also curious if Redwood Dedicated is required or if hosted will meet our throughput.
[00:47] Maya: good Q, for the pilot we usually start on hosted to move fast, but if you need guaranteed throughput / data isolation we can spin up a Dedicated pool. there are tradeoffs on cost and latency.
[00:58] Priya: for production we'll aim for dedicated, but for the poc, hosted is fine as long as we can get reproducible latency numbers. main goal is p90 under 300ms for short prompts and under 800ms for 8k context.
[01:12] Diego: noted. we'll measure p50/p90/p99 and throughput. plan is to run 1k requests at representative load and share a benchmark spreadsheet.
[01:21] Liam: for the VPC, we need to know whether you require full VPC peering or if shared transit VPC is an option; and also what ports/protocols.
[01:29] Maya: Diego, do we have a VPC playbook link? I can share a doc.
[01:33] Diego: yes, I'll drop the V-P-C peering guide in chat after the call, includes CIDR, ports, and route table examples.
[01:40] Sara: on security, we need SOC2, encryption at rest details, key management (KMS/HSM) and retention for logs. also audit trails for model versioning and who accessed tokens.
[01:51] Ethan: (interject) we have a security whitepaper and a SOC2 cert, and we can provide redacted audit logs. we'll share the links.
[01:58] Priya: perfect, also can you confirm data retention for logs from the hosted environment? we need 90 days by policy.
[02:05] Maya: Redwood hosted default is 30 days but enterprise controls can extend retention; I'll include options and pricing.
[02:12] Jamal: on IAM, we'll need a service account with restricted roles. can you give exact IAM permissions so we can scope least-privilege?
[02:20] Diego: yes, we have an IAM matrix. I'll attach it. small caveat, the initial setup requires broader rights to provision peering, but after that we can tighten.
[02:30] Priya: about model variants, can we test smaller quantized variants to compare cost vs latency? we want to see quality delta too.
[02:37] Diego: absolutely, we'll run the same prompt set on a float16 baseline and a 4-bit quantized variant. quality metrics will be in the spreadsheet — basic token-level diffs plus semantic scoring.
[02:47] Liam: for benchmarking, do you simulate concurrency or just sequential? our production will be bursty.
[02:52] Diego: we'll do both: steady-state throughput and burst patterns; we'll note batching parameters. also note that prefix/KV caching can affect p90 for repeated sessions.
[03:05] Sara: one more security note — we need SAML SSO for the console and RBAC for team roles.
[03:12] Ethan: SAML + RBAC supported; I'll send setup steps and a short demo doc.
[03:18] Priya: timeline — if you can run the benchmark by next Tuesday that'd be great. results will decide whether we move to Dedicated in the next phase.
[03:26] Maya: yes aiming for Tue/Wed. Diego, you okay to run?
[03:29] Diego: yep I'll run the 1k test with 8k context and attach the raw logs. I'll include p50/p90/p99 and cost per 1k tokens estimate.
[03:38] Jamal: I'll confirm account IDs and CIDR by Friday.
[03:42] Maya: perfect. any blockers on credentials?
[03:45] Jamal: we need the Redwood service account email and the exact steps; otherwise no blocker.
[03:50] Diego: I'll add the service account details to the peering guide, plus a sample terraform snippet.
[03:58] Priya: are there any limits on context length for hosted? you said 8k is fine?
[04:03] Diego: hosted supports 8k, above that we have to look at model compatibility and tokenization; Dedicated can be configured for longer contexts but requires more provisioning.
[04:14] Sara: on encryption — if we use hosted, keys are managed by Redwood by default, but can we bring our own KMS?
[04:22] Maya: BYOK is supported for Dedicated and for some hosted tiers via KMS integration; I'll confirm which plan supports BYOK and put that in the follow-up.
[04:31] Liam: also, network egress costs — can you share a rough estimate for 1M tokens?
[04:36] Ethan: we'll provide an estimate in the follow-up; depends on model size and batching, but we'll give a ballpark.
[04:43] Priya: ok great. last thing, can we get a quick demo of the console trace and per-token cost breakdown?
[04:48] Maya: yes we can record a 10-min demo and drop the link.
[04:52] Diego: also note, for reproducibility use the same seed and deterministic sampling for the benchmark. we'll include that in the test plan.
[04:59] Priya: thanks everyone.
[05:01] Maya: recap / next steps — Diego runs benchmarks by 9/29, Maya/Ethan send SOC2 and security docs by 9/25, Jamal to confirm VPC details by 9/26, Priya to share final prompt set by 9/28. follow-up meeting next week same time unless anyone needs earlier.
[05:20] End of recording.

References shared during call:
- Redwood VPC peering guide (link to be sent)
- SOC2 + security whitepaper (link)
- Benchmark spreadsheet template (to be populated by SE)
- Sample IAM matrix and terraform snippet (to be attached)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-hear of product names (e.g., 'Redwood Dedicated' as 'Redwood Dedicate') and VPC sometimes transcribed as 'V-P-C' or 'VPCK' in parts.
